_note: se MANUFACTURING CAPABILITIES — versioned DATA, one row per (process, material), the file se-kind.md's 'Manufacturing modes' section specifies. SEEDED NARROWLY on 2026-09-15 by docs/backlog/se-off-the-shelf-fabrication.md rung 3c, which needed three fields and refused to hardcode them: a printed hole comes out undersize, so a core hole sized straight from the thread-forming table splits the boss it is in. The full field set (layer height, overhang angle, bridge span, bed contact, anisotropic strength vector, CNC/SLA/laser families) belongs to se-kind.md slice 5 and is NOT here yet — an absent field is absent, never a figure carried over from a neighbouring row. Every length is MILLIMETRES. TWO TIERS per field, as that section requires: `physical` is the floor the process cannot go below whatever anyone declares, `house` is what we actually build to, at a margin. A consumer reads through one resolver and clamps to `physical`. CONFIDENCE: these are community FDM practice for a 0.4 mm nozzle at 0.2 mm layers, NOT measurements from this shop's printers — the honest thing to do with them is calibrate once and override, which is why every row says so in its own source.

rows.title: FDM, PLA — 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer

hole_diameter_compensation.source: A vertical hole prints undersize: the extrusion's inside corner is laid on a polygon that cuts the circle, and the melt shrinks inward. +0.2 mm on the modelled diameter is the common community compensation for a 0.4 mm nozzle; the physical floor is 0, which is what a perfectly calibrated machine with hole compensation in the slicer needs. NOT measured here.

min_wall.source: One extrusion line at 0.42 mm (1.05 x nozzle) is the physical floor; two perimeters is the house minimum for anything structural.

min_boss_wall.source: A boss that a thread is formed into carries hoop stress, so it wants three perimeters rather than two. House rule, not measured.

rows.title: FDM, PETG — 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer

hole_diameter_compensation.source: As fdm/pla, plus a little: PETG oozes and rounds inside corners more, so holes close up further. NOT measured here.

min_boss_wall.source: As fdm/pla; PETG's higher layer adhesion helps a formed thread rather than hurting it.

rows.title: FDM, ABS — 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer, enclosed

hole_diameter_compensation.source: As fdm/pla plus shrinkage on cooling (ABS shrinks ~0.5-0.8% and a small hole shrinks with the part). NOT measured here.

rows.title: FDM, ASA — 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer, enclosed

hole_diameter_compensation.source: As fdm/abs — same chemistry family, same shrinkage order. NOT measured here.

rows.title: FDM, TPU — 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.2 mm layer

hole_diameter_compensation.source: Flexible filament is extruded slowly and springs back, so holes close up more than in a rigid material. NOT measured here.

min_wall.source: A thin TPU wall is floppy rather than broken, so the minimum is a stiffness judgement, not a printability one.

min_boss_wall.source: A thread formed in TPU deflects instead of gripping; if a joint needs one, it wants noticeably more material around it. House judgement.
